blocks.content: Latitudes determine climatic zones across the globe, whereas longitudes are essential for determining local time and time zones.

rows: East to West, parallel to Equator
North to South, converging at Poles
Maximum at Equator (~111 km), zero at Poles

items: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82°30' E longitude, which passes through Mirzapur (UP) and is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Every 1° longitude shift causes a 4-minute time difference (15° = 1 hour).
Crossing the International Date Line (180° Longitude) from West to East gains a calendar day, whereas crossing from East to West loses a day.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Latitudes are parallel horizontal lines that measure angular distance north or south of the Equator.
Longitudes are vertical semi-circles running from pole to pole that measure angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.
The distance between any two parallel latitudes remains constant across the globe at approximately 111 km.
Longitudes converge at the poles, meaning the distance between them is maximum at the Equator and decreases to zero at the poles.
Longitudes are fundamentally used to calculate local time, where 15 degrees of longitude corresponds to a time difference of 1 hour.
